legend: You are given a positive integer n%%ZSMJ0%%.
Find a sequence of fractions aibi%%ZSMJ1%%, i=1…k%%ZSMJ2%% (where ai%%ZSMJ3%% and bi%%ZSMJ4%% are positive integers) for some k%%ZSMJ5%% such that:
{bi divides n, 1<bi<n for i=1…k1≤ai<bi for i=1…kk∑i=1aibi=1−1n%%ZSMJ6%%
input: The input consists of a single integer n%%ZSMJ7%% (2≤n≤109%%ZSMJ8%%).

If there exists such a sequence, next lines should contain a description of the sequence in the following format.

The second line should contain integer k%%ZSMJ9%% (1≤k≤100000%%ZSMJ10%%) — the number of elements in the sequence. It is guaranteed that if such a sequence exists, then there exists a sequence of length at most 100000%%ZSMJ11%%.

note: In the second example there is a sequence 12,13%%ZSMJ15%% such that 12+13=1−16%%ZSMJ16%%.
